meta.notes: 0 sub-tags had no generated definition and were stubbed; 24 config-only 9012 keys documented from the rule files.

parsing.aliasResolution: A 9012 key may be the number or the alphabetic alias taken from the method name __p_<number>_<ALIAS>; both are stored in the tag map, so tag9012(1546) and tag9012(PQS) return the same value. Numbers >= 1500 are engine-internal. Keys with no parser (e.g. AUCTIONS, OCTC, TROWESWITCH, IGNORE_ARROWST_CHECK, USEDLP, BADSSR, NOPOST) are kept verbatim as 'unknown key' and are only visible to config rule conditions.
parsing.expressionValues: A value starting with '$' is evaluated as an expression (top-level tags unless listed in noeval_fixtags, default '58 109 116 9603 9604'; 9012 sub-tags unless in noeval_9012tags).
parsing.paramGenerator: A 9012 key starting with pgen_char (default '!') is a parameter generator: the generator's output (a ^-list) replaces the key/value in place.
steps: stripFixTags: split on ';', each token split on the first '=' into key/value; empty values are dropped; a repeated top-level tag overwrites the earlier one EXCEPT 9012, whose repeats are concatenated with '^' (Parameters.java:10619-10657).
9050/9052 are appended to the 9012 value already seen, WITHOUT a '^' separator; if 9050/9052 occurs before any 9012 in the string its value is discarded (Parameters.java:10636-10643).

client order id from client_oid_tag (default 9604) or alt_client_oid_tag, client id from clientid_tag (default 109), staff id from staffid_tag (default 116); all top-level tags are kept in _fixtagmap (Parameters.java:11235-11267, AlgoConfig.java:3391-3400).
9060 + 9065 + 9066 are concatenated (no separator) into the sub-parameter string (Parameters.java:11270-11276).
parse900Tags: 9009 (open/close flags), 9001 (algorithm, via algo_shorthand_map), 9002/9003 (start/end; an 'x-HH:MM:SS' value keeps only the part after '-'), 9008 basket (Parameters.java:10680-10727).
9012 from this message is appended after any earlier 9012 (_tag9012 + '^' + new) so later segments win (Parameters.java:11278).
processAlgorithm: working algorithm = 9012 sub-tag 1 (ALGO) if seen, else 9001; may be converted by OPE scheduler / algo relay map (Parameters.java:10924-10961).
parseGreekTags: 9004-9007 (alpha/beta/gamma/delta) are mapped to algorithm-specific fields (Parameters.java:10758-10922).
parse9012: sub-tags split on '^' (honouring <tq>..</tq> quotes), each applied in order by its __p_ parser; later occurrences overwrite earlier ones (Parameters.java:1390-1484).

computeRelayAlgorithm (non-final), then every rule of ai.fixmsg.properties is evaluated top to bottom; each matching rule's fixmsg is re-parsed into the order immediately (combine_fix_msg_config=false) so last writer wins and later rules see earlier writes (FixMsgConfig.java:101-199).
9060 handling: COMPOUND -> compound config; 58/61=CUSTOM -> custom-convert config; otherwise -> sub-order parameters (setSubParameters) (Parameters.java:11340-11349).
CUSTOM conversion (58/61 starting with 'C'), validity check (invalid algorithm -> error), final relay computation, parametersFinalProcess, adjust (Parameters.java:11351-11408).
Errors: _err_msg or a KO (9012.1525) value makes checkForError() return a reject reason; the order is rejected (Parameters.java:12737-12745, FlexOrderStream.java:13330-13333).
parsing.notes: Rule file syntax: '<fixmsg> :: cond1, cond2, ...' (ConfigFilter with '::' and ','); optional 'IR=<n>;' prefix restricts a rule by relay state (0: order not relayed, 1: relayed, 2: parent not relayed, 3: parent relayed; FixMsgConfig.java:116-131,211-216). '<js>..</js>' fragments in the fixmsg or conditions are JavaScript evaluated with _param/_stock bound. Rules are skipped entirely for TESTORDER/FORCEORDER/PATH (FixMsgConfig.java:103).

tags.name: HandlInst
tags.description: Client-FIX tag extracted by kdb post-trade from the raw ('|'-delimited) client FIX message of ARROWST orders into column HandInst. No engine code reads it from the order fixmsg; the order-monitor notes list it among tags that change behaviour, which the engine source does not confirm.

tags.name: Text
tags.description: Standard FIX free-text field. The only engine reference is the default noeval_fixtags list, so a value starting with '$' is kept as literal text instead of being evaluated. No other engine logic reading top-level 58 was found. (A Parameters.java comment mentions 'tag 58/61' for CUSTOM conversion, but that refers to 9012 sub-tags.)

example.explanation: Kept as the literal '$see desk' because 58 is in noeval_fixtags.

interactions.title: Tag 58 values starting with '$' are not evaluated
interactions.explanation: When the fixmsg is parsed, any top-level value that starts with '$' is evaluated as an expression by ConfigFilter, unless the tag is listed in noeval_fixtags. The default list is '58 109 116 9603 9604', so a '$' value in tag 58 is kept as literal text. The deployed ai.server.properties does not override noeval_fixtags.

tags.name: Settlement type
tags.description: Client-FIX tag extracted by kdb post-trade from the raw ('|'-delimited) client FIX message of ARROWST orders into column settlementTyp. No engine code reads it from the order fixmsg; the order-monitor notes list it among tags that change behaviour, which the engine source does not confirm.

tags.name: Settlement date
tags.description: Client-FIX tag extracted by kdb post-trade from the raw ('|'-delimited) client FIX message of ARROWST orders into column settlementDate. No engine code reads it from the order fixmsg; the order-monitor notes list it among tags that change behaviour, which the engine source does not confirm.

tags.name: ClientID
tags.description: Client identifier (standard FIX ClientID). The engine reads it through the config key clientid_tag (default 109) and stores it as Parameters._clientid. That value is then used for per-client venue/broker maps, for self-cross identification, for OMS 'target_client' records, and as a condition (fixTag(109)) in ai.fixmsg.properties rules. If the tag is missing, the client ID comes from the ClientInfo config entry for the striped basket ID (9008).
tags.default: none; falls back to ClientInfo.clientID() looked up by the striped basket id (Parameters.java:11260-11266)

example.explanation: Sets client GRANTHAM. With queue_mode>0 and a max participation level below 50, the rule file adds 9012 144=1.

interactions.title: GRANTHAM orders get 9012 144=1 when part-level capped
interactions.explanation: For client GRANTHAM with queue_mode>0, maxPartLevel (or maxLitPartLevel, in a second rule) between 0 and 50, and no 144 set, the rule adds 9012 144=1.

interactions.title: ELKCAP orders with 9012 55 get LCR=0.05 outside JP
interactions.explanation: For client ELKCAP, outside JP, when 9012 tag 55 is set and LCR is not, the rule adds LCR=0.05.

interactions.title: Non-ELKCAP orders with 9012 55 get LCR=0.05 (except IN / 155=SG)
interactions.explanation: For every client other than ELKCAP, when 9012 55 is set, LCR is unset, 155 is not SG and the market is not IN, the rule adds LCR=0.05. A separate JP rule adds LCR=0.05 for non-ELKCAP orders when 155!=SG, even if 55 is not set.

interactions.title: STEWFS orders get a default 9012 70
interactions.explanation: For client STEWFS with no 70, the rule sets 70=S,B,500. For an unpriced order that has not opened yet (price<0.00001, opened<1), the preceding rule sets 70=C,B,500. Both rules match such an order and the last writer wins (S,B,500).

interactions.title: 109 is copied into sub-parameter / converted orders
interactions.explanation: When a sub-parameter set (9060/compound legs) is built, or an order is converted by a CUSTOM rule, the tags in subparam_oldfixtags (default '109,9008') are copied into the new fixmsg. The client ID therefore stays on the child legs.

interactions.title: Client order id is composed with client ID
interactions.explanation: With client_oid_include_clientid enabled (default 0), clientOrderID() returns <9604>_<clientID>_<symbol>. In chain mode it returns <refid>_<clientID>_<algo>_<symbol>.

interactions.title: Tag 109 values starting with '$' are not evaluated
interactions.explanation: When the fixmsg is parsed, any top-level value that starts with '$' is evaluated as an expression by ConfigFilter, unless the tag is listed in noeval_fixtags. The default list is '58 109 116 9603 9604', so a '$' value in tag 109 is kept as literal text. The deployed ai.server.properties does not override noeval_fixtags.

tags.name: OnBehalfOfCompID (sender)
tags.description: Client-FIX tag extracted by kdb post-trade from the raw ('|'-delimited) client FIX message of ARROWST orders into column tag115 / SenderCompID. No engine code reads it from the order fixmsg; the order-monitor notes list it among tags that change behaviour, which the engine source does not confirm.

tags.name: Staff / trader ID (OnBehalfOfSubID)
tags.description: Trader or staff identifier. The engine reads it through the config key staffid_tag (default 116) and stores it as Parameters._staffid. It is written to the OMS 'target_client' record as traderID and copied to the portfolio together with the client ID. If the tag is missing, the value comes from the ClientInfo entry for the striped basket ID, but only when 109 is also missing. Standard FIX 116 is OnBehalfOfSubID; the 'staff' meaning comes from the engine's config key name.

example.explanation: Recorded as traderID for this order in OMS.

tags.name: Algorithm (client strategy)
tags.description: Names the client algorithm. Resolved through algo_shorthand_map (e.g. V->VWAP, S->SHADOW) and Algorithm.getAlgorithm (prefix matches for COMPOUND*/CUSTOM*/...; SWITCHER->COMPOUND). Kept as clientAlgorithm/tag9001; the working algorithm can be overridden by 9012 sub-tag 1 (ALGO) and by config rules.

allowedValues.meaning: TMX variant: if the stock comes back into limit, re-schedules over the remaining time instead of catching up to the original profile.
Volume-weighted scheduled algo following the volume profile; isVwap/isScheduled.
Dark-liquidity seeking algo (requires dark pools); uses venue bits.
Opportunistic liquidity-seeking algo (likeNinja); uses venue bits.
Participation within a min/max rate band ('line').
'Work Or Wait' style i-would algo: 9005 = max work part rate, 9007 = i-would bps (0 -> default bps).
Participation-capped algo (needs volume events and profile).
Portfolio-level cash-balanced algo (needDoCash, portfolio_level_algos default CASH FALL PAIR PORT).
Cash-balancing portfolio algo; 9006 gamma = cash ratio, 9007 delta = cash tolerance.
Direct market access; uses client limit (useClientLimit).
Smart open-auction algo; used for SMART_OPEN relay children when 217 (moo rate type)>0 and the stock has not opened.
Implementation-shortfall style algo; must-complete by default; with MOC forms the 'Indian close' family.
Multi-leg algo: switches between child algos per 9060 config; mode chosen by 9012.139 (1/6/7 position, 2/3 time, 5 portfolio/pair, other <100 price/algo tracker, named JS trigger -> 100).
Price-scaling algo; requires scale start/end price, step size or increment (9012.100/101/109/102).
Compound VWAP (any name starting with COMPOUNDVWAP).
Custom conversion algo: with 9012.58 or 9012.61 = 'CUSTOM' the 9060 thresholds choose the real algo by %ADV or market cap; 61=C-TSW uses a fixed TSW table.
Ladder algo (price ladder); 9012.197 builds a compound config.
Relative-performance LINE (impact child algo); impact child algo that exists in the scheduler; handles execution style (provide vs take) via aggression.
Relative LINE using historical reference; impact child algo that exists in the scheduler; handles execution style (provide vs take) via aggression.
Relative LINE on-the-day reference; impact child algo that exists in the scheduler; handles execution style (provide vs take) via aggression.
Relative VWAP (scheduled relative); impact child algo that exists in the scheduler; handles execution style (provide vs take) via aggression.
Relative TMX; impact child algo that exists in the scheduler; handles execution style (provide vs take) via aggression.
Impact child algo: NINJA whose limit price is a function of moving averages etc.
Participation rate based on market cap, so the rate varies within a basket; 9005 beta = lit target/max/min, 9004 alpha = lit range.
SHADOW with a minimum participation rate.
OPE split leg of SHADOW (not in scheduler).
OPE split leg of SHADOW (not in scheduler).
OPE split leg of SHADOW (not in scheduler).
OPE split leg of VWAP (split_parameter, e.g. VWAP=OPEVWAP1,OPEVWAP2).
OPE split leg of VWAP (split_parameter, e.g. VWAP=OPEVWAP1,OPEVWAP2).
OPE split leg of VWAP (split_parameter, e.g. VWAP=OPEVWAP1,OPEVWAP2).
OPE split leg of VWAP (split_parameter, e.g. VWAP=OPEVWAP1,OPEVWAP2).
OPE split leg of VWAP (split_parameter, e.g. VWAP=OPEVWAP1,OPEVWAP2).
OPE split leg of VWAP (split_parameter, e.g. VWAP=OPEVWAP1,OPEVWAP2).
DMA using client-input iceberg size combined with stop-loss and limit price.
VWAP run in the OPE scheduler (target of OPE conversion of VWAP).
TMX run in the OPE scheduler.
Smart order router algo; no scheduler, zero portfolio delay.
Path through to order types, like TESTORDER but checks venue shutoff; config rules are not applied to test algos.
Test algo sending shares to an order type; skips market data and config rules.
Same as TESTORDER, different name for compliance reporting.
Sends a resting order at the client limit; skips market data.
Target-close with a different scheduler base; OPE sends the remainder to MOC.
Shell algo for tag-driven features; no scheduler.
Direct Limit Post; no scheduler; MOC disabled for orders from DLP; may leave during lunch break.

tags.name: Start time
tags.description: Order start time (HH:MM:SS, exchange-local). A value 'x-HH:MM:SS' keeps only the part after '-'. Overridden by 9012 sub-tag 2 (which also accepts relative '30s'/'5m'/'1h' offsets).

example.explanation: Start trading at 09:30.

tags.name: End time
tags.description: Order end time. Same format as 9002. Overridden by 9012 sub-tag 3.

example.explanation: Finish by 16:00.

tags.name: Alpha (greek 1)
tags.description: Generic numeric parameter whose meaning depends on the algorithm (mostly aggression, -1..1). Superseded by 9012.4 when both present (9012 is parsed after the greeks).

example.explanation: For VWAP: aggression 0.5.

tags.name: Beta (greek 2)
tags.description: Generic numeric parameter; for schedule/participation algos the max (or target) participation rate in %, for SHADOW/NINJA the venue bit mask.

example.explanation: For VWAP: max 20% of volume.

tags.name: Gamma (greek 3)
tags.description: Generic numeric parameter; i-would level for PCAP/LINE/passive algos, max lit part for NINJA, cash ratio for CASH.

example.explanation: For NINJA: max lit participation 10%.

tags.name: Delta (greek 4)
tags.description: Generic parameter; i-would for scheduled/PART algos (Y/T=1, N/F=0), max part for LINE/PCAP/passive, min part for SHADOW, i-would bps for WOW, cash tolerance for CASH.

example.explanation: For LINE: max 25% of volume.

tags.name: Basket id
tags.description: Basket/portfolio id; a striped version (stripedBasketID) is used by config rules and to look up client/staff ids when 109/116 are absent. Rejected as 'unknown basket id' when empty.

example.explanation: Arrowstreet basket; triggers ARROWST rules.

tags.name: Auction participation flag
tags.description: 1 = do open auction, 2 = do close auction, 3 = both. It can only switch participation ON (doopen/doclose=1); 0 or absence does not switch off. has9009 condition is true whenever the tag is present.

allowedValues.meaning: no explicit auction (no effect in code)

example.explanation: Participate in the close auction.

tags.name: Sender sub id
tags.description: Constant exists (_CSENDER_SUBID_PARAMETER) but the engine takes senderSubID from the FIX order descriptor, not from the fixmsg; reading 9010 from fixmsg was not found. ORDER-MONITOR-DATA-MODEL.md:240 calls 9010 'Would-Good-Price / iwould', which the engine source does not support.

tags.name: Algo parameter container
tags.description: Container of '^'-separated sub-tags 'key=value' (key = number or alias). Repeated 9012 tags and 9050/9052 are merged into it; config rules append their own 9012 after the client's so later values win. Values may be quoted with <tq>..</tq>, '$' expressions, or '!' parameter generators.

example.explanation: Queue mode off; post at most half the quote size.

tags.name: 9012 extension 1
tags.description: Extra sub-tags appended to 9012. The value is concatenated directly onto the 9012 value already parsed (no '^' inserted) and is lost if it appears before 9012 in the string.

example.explanation: Needs a leading '^' to form a separate sub-tag.

tags.name: 9012 extension 2
tags.description: Same as 9050.

tags.name: Sub-parameters / compound config
tags.description: For COMPOUND: the compound config (header,threshold_algoparams,...), e.g. 'T,08:00:00_1=SMOO^217=1,08:30:00_1=LINE'. For 58/61=CUSTOM: conversion thresholds. Otherwise: parameters for the relayed sub-order. 9065 and 9066 are concatenated onto it. If absent, 9012 sub-tag 60 is used with '~'->'=' and '|'->'^'. Must be >= 5 chars to be used.

example.explanation: Time-based compound: VWAP from 10:00, LINE from 12:00 (with 9001=COMPOUND, 139=3).

tags.name: Sub-parameter continuation 1
tags.description: Concatenated (no separator) onto 9060.

tags.name: Sub-parameter continuation 2
tags.description: Concatenated (no separator) onto 9060 after 9065.

tags.name: ClOrderID (client order reference)
tags.description: Client order reference stored in the target fixmsg. KDB post-trade and reporting scripts read it as ClOrderID to join targets to client new-order messages. The engine itself only names it in the default noeval_fixtags list, so a '$' value is not evaluated. It is not the default client_oid_tag (that is 9604), but it could be configured through client_oid_tag or alt_client_oid_tag.

example.explanation: Used in reports to match the algo target to the client's order.

tags.name: Client order ID
tags.description: Client order identifier. The engine reads it through the config key client_oid_tag (default 9604); if it is missing, the alt_client_oid_tag (default empty) is tried. The trimmed value is stored as Parameters._client_oid. The engine uses it to key _clientordermap, to find the head order of a chain order, to resolve the old order on a modify (IDMOD lookup), and as id_client in OMS client-state records.

example.explanation: Later amendments that refer to ORD123456 are matched to this algo order.

interactions.title: Modify requests resolve the old order via client order id
interactions.explanation: When a new target carries IDMOD, the engine looks up the order in _clientordermap (which is keyed by clientOrderID()) and, if found, replaces that order.

interactions.title: Chain orders link to their head via client order id
interactions.explanation: In chain-order mode, if no id_target is given, the engine looks up the existing chain order by client order id.

tags.name: Modified order ID (replace target)
tags.description: ID of the order that this target replaces. The engine sets it when it processes a replace (setIdMod), and the value is also accepted as 9012 sub-tag 1543/IDMOD. setIdMod also adds a top-level 'IDMOD' key to the fixtag map if it is not already there, so it appears in OMS target_tags. A new target with an IDMOD and no old order is handled as a modify: the old order is found by client order id and then replaced.
tags.valueFormat: order id or client order id

example.explanation: This target replaces algo order 10234.

interactions.title: IDMOD turns a new target into a replace
interactions.explanation: If idMod() is set and there is no old order yet, onNewTarget calls replaceTargetOrder for the referenced order instead of creating an independent order.

tags.name: Algorithm override
tags.description: Sets the algorithm inside 9012, replacing the algorithm from 9001 (client algo). The value is upper-cased and passed through the shorthand map (algo_from_shorthand); an unknown/invalid name is silently ignored and the previous algorithm is kept. The whole tag is ignored when the OEO config lists the current algorithm in no_algo_tag. It also derives the impact algorithm (e.g. SHADOW1/2/3 -> SHADOW, VWAP1..3/OPEVWAPn -> VWAP, ICEDMA -> SDMA).

example.explanation: Run the order as PASS regardless of the 9001 algorithm.

interactions.title: 9012 ALGO beats 9001
interactions.explanation: __p_1_ALGO assigns _algorithm directly while parsing 9012, which happens after 9001 has been read (parse900Tags/processAlgorithm), so a valid sub-tag 1 replaces the 9001 algorithm and any relay conversion computed from it. Greek tags 9004-9007 are mapped using the algorithm in effect before 9012 is parsed, and are re-parsed only when the 9012 algo differs from the client algo (parsegreek).

interactions.title: Ignored for algorithms listed in no_algo_tag
interactions.explanation: If Util.getOEOConfig().no_algo_tag(<current algorithm>) is true the tag is not applied at all.

interactions.title: Config converts limit DMA orders to DLP
interactions.explanation: Rules write 1=DLP^104=1^AUNS=1 for SDMA/DMA(/ICEDMA) limit orders starting before the close when USEDLP is 1 (DMA/SDMA) or 2 (incl. ICEDMA).

interactions.title: Client templates keyed on tag 88 rewrite the algorithm
interactions.explanation: Several rules use the value of sub-tag 88 as a template key and write ALGO=LINE (88=MFSIS), ALGO=PASS (88=PORT with 9001=FALL), ALGO=VWAP (88=SgaMoc) or ALGO=SHADOW (88=APSHADOWn) together with other parameters.

interactions.title: Order rejected if final algorithm is invalid
interactions.explanation: After parsing, an invalid final algorithm sets _err_msg 'invalid algorithm'. Note an invalid sub-tag 1 value is itself ignored, so this only fires when 9001 is also invalid.

tags.name: Start time / start offset after open
tags.description: Order start time. A value ending in s/m/h is an offset from the continuous-session open (e.g. 30s, 5m, 1h) stored as start_open; otherwise it is parsed as a clock time (like 9002) and flagged for timezone conversion. Because 9012 is parsed after 9002, this replaces the 9002 start time.

example.explanation: Start 5 minutes after the continuous open.

interactions.title: Sub-tag 2 replaces 9002
interactions.explanation: Both set _startstamp/_tag9002; 9002 is parsed in parse900Tags before 9012, so the 9012 value wins.

interactions.title: Offset start disables do-open
interactions.explanation: When the start is an offset after the open (start_open>0) the opening-auction participation computed from 14/9009 is cleared (customtags_open=0), and ExecutionOptimizer sets the start to open+offset.

interactions.title: Config clears 217/218/219 when start is before MOO
interactions.explanation: Rule writes 217=0^218=0^219=0 when 217 is set, tag 2 is present and start_to_moo>0.

tags.name: End time
tags.description: Order end time as a clock time (same parsing as 9003), flagged for timezone conversion. Parsed after 9003 so it replaces it. Inside a compound leg (9060) it ends that leg at a clock time.

example.explanation: Stop scheduling at 14:30 local time.

interactions.title: Sub-tag 3 replaces 9003
interactions.explanation: Both set _endstamp/_tag9003; 9003 is parsed first in parse900Tags, so the 9012 value wins.

interactions.title: Close tag with early end time is rejected
interactions.explanation: With 15=1 and an end time before the closing auction end (and reset_close_endstamp==0 for the stock) the order is rejected 'in close tag conflict with endstamp'.

interactions.title: End time decides close participation in EU/US
interactions.explanation: In the EU region an end at/after continuous end turns do-close on, an earlier end turns it off (unless moc_rate_type>=20); with 9009 in other regions the end vs closing-auction begin decides close participation.

tags.name: Aggression
tags.description: Aggressiveness level of the algo in [-1, 1] (negative = more passive, positive = more aggressive). Used throughout candidate sizing and venue logic (e.g. SHADOW with aggression < -0.5 shrinks workable size, NINJA with aggression >= 1 behaves aggressively, qmoc close rate shifts by 20*aggression).

example.explanation: Fairly passive execution.

interactions.title: Sub-tag 4 beats 9004 alpha
interactions.explanation: parseGreekTags copies 9004 (alpha) into _aggression for these algos; 9012 is parsed afterwards so sub-tag 4 wins.

interactions.title: Aggression below -1 rejected
interactions.explanation: checkForError returns 'aggression out of range' when aggression < -1 or > 1.

interactions.title: Aggression above 1 rejected
interactions.explanation: checkForError returns 'aggression out of range' when aggression > 1.

interactions.title: Aggressive NINJA cannot use cash balance
interactions.explanation: checkForError rejects 'aggressive NINJA with Cash feature' when a NINJA-like algo has aggression>0 and cash balancing is on.

tags.name: Min participation rate
tags.description: Minimum participation rate in percent of market volume. For SHADOW-family algos it is the minimum rate (9007 delta maps here), for LINE/PART 9005 beta maps here. Validated against configured bounds.
tags.default: 0 (none); when this tag is absent: GNR conversion defaults 5=8 / 6=25 (Parameters.java:12591)

example.explanation: Participate at least 5% of volume.

algorithmDependent.behavior: Ignored: minPartLevel() returns the target rate (tag 7) and parse9012 overwrites _minpartlevel with the target.

interactions.title: Ignored for PART (target rate used)
interactions.explanation: After 9012 parsing PART sets min=max=target part level, and minPartLevel() returns _targetpartlevel for PART.

interactions.title: Min rate above max rate rejected
interactions.explanation: checkForError: 'min part level > max part level' when both >0 and min>max.

interactions.title: Min rate <=1% cannot be combined with dark only
interactions.explanation: checkForError rejects a min part level in (0,1] when Dark Only (37=1) is set.

interactions.title: Rate outside configured bounds rejected
interactions.explanation: Rejected when min part level > min(100, minpart_reject) or below min(1, minpart_reject_min).

interactions.title: BernX-only cannot combine with min part
interactions.explanation: checkForError: 'BernX-only cannot combine with iwould or min part' when internal cross is 2.

tags.name: Max participation rate
tags.description: Maximum participation rate (volume cap) in percent of market volume. 9005 beta (VWAP/TMX/PART/FALL/CASH) or 9007 delta (LINE/PCAP/SMKT/IIS/SMALL/PASS/GNR) map here; sub-tag 6 is parsed later and wins.

example.explanation: Never exceed 20% of market volume.

algorithmDependent.behavior: Ignored: maxPartLevel() returns the target rate (tag 7).
Ignored: maxPartLevel() returns tag 16 (max work part rate).

interactions.title: Ignored for PART
interactions.explanation: maxPartLevel() returns _targetpartlevel for PART and parse9012 overwrites _maxpartlevel with the target.

interactions.title: Ignored for WOW (tag 16 used)
interactions.explanation: maxPartLevel() returns _maxworkpartrate for WOW.

interactions.title: Max rate outside configured bounds rejected
interactions.explanation: Rejected when > min(100, maxpart_reject) or >0 and < min(1, maxpart_reject_min).

interactions.title: Max rate disables default must-complete
interactions.explanation: mustComplete() defaults to the algorithm's default only when maxPartLevel()<=0; setting 6 makes the order not must-complete unless 23=1.

interactions.title: China: volume cap with must-complete is KO'd
interactions.explanation: Config rule writes KO 'Volume cap ... conflicting with Must Complete 23=1' for China.

interactions.title: Config defaults 6=50 for adaptive LINE
interactions.explanation: LINE with index-tracker adaption 1/2/5/6 and no max rate gets 6=50.

tags.name: Target participation rate
tags.description: Target participation rate in percent. For PART it is the participation rate (min and max are both set to it); for PART2 it sets the lit target rate instead. For other algos it sets targetPartLevel (also used as the default MOC part level).

example.explanation: PART: participate at 10% of volume.

algorithmDependent.behavior: Sets the participation rate; min=max=target after parsing; 9005 beta also maps here.
Sets the lit target rate (_targetlitpartlevel); min/max lit = target; halved for small caps / large %ADV (see 58/61).

interactions.title: PART without a positive rate rejected
interactions.explanation: checkForError: 'part rate <= 0' when PART and minPartLevel()<=0 (which is the target).

interactions.title: PART target replaces min/max
interactions.explanation: parse9012 sets _maxpartlevel=_minpartlevel=_targetpartlevel for PART (and lit levels for PART2).

interactions.title: Meaning depends on algorithm at parse time
interactions.explanation: __p_7 checks _algorithm == PART2 while parsing; the lit vs non-lit field chosen depends on the algorithm in effect when tag 7 is read.

interactions.title: India IIS->VWAP clears target
interactions.explanation: Config rule writes 7=0 for IN orders whose 9001 is IIS but run as VWAP with a target rate.

tags.name: Participation range
tags.description: Allowed band around the target participation rate (percent). For PART sets partRange; for PART2 sets the lit part range. 9004 alpha maps here for PART/PART2.

example.explanation: Allow +/-2% around the target rate.

algorithmDependent.behavior: Sets _litpartrange; halved together with lit rates for small caps / large %ADV.

tags.name: Max lit participation rate
tags.description: Maximum participation rate on lit venues (percent). For NINJA/ICENINJA 9006 gamma maps here; for PART2 9005 beta maps here (and tag 7 overwrites it). Used to cap lit shares per period.

example.explanation: At most 10% of volume on lit venues.

interactions.title: Lit max above max rate rejected
interactions.explanation: checkForError: 'max lit part level > max part level'.

interactions.title: Out of bounds rejected
interactions.explanation: Rejected when > min(100,maxpart_reject) or >0 and too small.

interactions.title: PART2: replaced by lit target
interactions.explanation: parse9012 sets _maxlitpartlevel=_targetlitpartlevel for PART2.

tags.name: Would price (I-would)
tags.description: Opportunistic 'would' price: when the market reaches it the algo trades more aggressively. Accepts an absolute price, or a relative spec parsed by IWouldPrice (e.g. B<bps> / C<cps> offsets as in 'B-10,3'). A value starting with 'M' and containing at least 3 ':'-separated fields is a multiple-would spec for the scheduler (mult_iwouldpmode=1). Ignored for WOW algos (non-M values).
tags.default: none (WOW: wow_default_wouldstr; SMKT: B-6); when this tag is absent: APIH: would % without 10/31 KO'd (ai.fixmsg.properties:475)

example.explanation: Would trigger 10 bps better than the reference (rule used in SSGA template).

tags.name: Scale step size

tags.name: Halt volume mode

tags.name: Anti-gaming venue type mode
tags.description: Which venue types to avoid for anti-gaming: 0 = use config (antigame_algos / antigame_venue_type), 1 = avoid periodic-mid venues, 2 = avoid pmid or dark, 3 = avoid pmid, dark or posting venues, 4 = avoid all.

example.explanation: Avoid pmid and dark venues.

tags.name: End time reject mode
tags.description: Controls rejecting/expiring the order after its end time: mode[,erb]. Mode <=1 also rejects unsent residual after the close; mode 1 measures to the (rolled) end stamp instead of the raw end; even modes reject EXPIRED after a buffer, odd modes reject SEND_ND_EXPIRED immediately; <= -100 disables the expiry reject. Second field (erb) is stored but not read elsewhere in this tree.
tags.default: -1 (config sets 3 when absent); when this tag is absent: Config default 112=3 (ai.fixmsg.properties:425, ai.fixmsg.properties:266, ai.fixmsg.properties:270, AI-FIXMSG-CONFLICTS.md:68)

example.explanation: Expire immediately after end time.

tags.name: Regulator halt threshold
tags.description: threshold[,mode]: pause the order when the price has moved more than the threshold (spread-normalised bps vs benchmark) from the strike; mode <1 lets candidates ignore the halt. Default comes from config for regulator_halt_algos.

tags.name: Regulator halt min periods
tags.description: Minimum duration (in OEO monitor periods) for the regulator halt logic; <=0 uses config.

tags.name: Regulator halt max periods
tags.description: Maximum duration (in OEO monitor periods) for the regulator halt logic; <=0 uses config.

tags.name: Adjust by beta
tags.description: >0 weights cash/portfolio balancing by the stock's equity beta (eqyBeta) instead of 1.

example.explanation: Beta-adjusted balance.

tags.name: Historical volume mode
tags.description: For LINE with index-tracker adaption (79) other than 3/4/7: >0 selects LINERELATIVE_HIST instead of LINERELATIVE as the impact child algo.
tags.default: 0; when this tag is absent: Config sets 117=1 for ARROWST (ai.fixmsg.properties:38)

tags.name: Index change volume mode
tags.description: >0 uses the index-change closing volume estimate (closingVolume(true)) for close sizing and caps.

tags.name: Index change volume
tags.description: Index-change volume factor; in this tree it is only read by its accessor and printed in the parameter dump. Effect unknown.

tags.name: Always post loud
tags.description: When 1, lit (displayed) posting is always allowed: ExchangeMaster picks aggression level POST instead of the region/ADV-based post-blind logic, PostWorker marks the order as able to post loud, and ConcertStrategy.noPostLoud() returns false (any value > 0) even for NINJA or clean-pipe 63 orders.

example.explanation: Allow displayed lit posts regardless of the post-blind rules.

algorithmDependent.behavior: NINJA normally never posts loud; with 120>0 noPostLoud() returns false before the NINJA check, so lit posting venues are set up.
ExchangeMaster's earlier NINJA/shadow branch (POSTBLIND) is evaluated before the 120 check, so the order-level aggression stays POSTBLIND for those cases.

interactions.title: 120 re-enables lit posting for NINJA and clean-pipe 63
interactions.explanation: ConcertStrategy.noPostLoud() checks always_post_loud first and returns false, so NINJA's and cleanPipe()==63's 'no post loud' rule (tag 213) is bypassed.

interactions.title: 120 does not change ExchangeMaster aggression for NINJA/shadow
interactions.explanation: In ExchangeMaster the NINJA / shadow (no min part or shadowmin_post_loud<=0) branch sets POSTBLIND before the always_post_loud==1 branch is reached.

tags.name: Random lot size
tags.description: Randomises the size of normal (non-auction) candidates by up to +/- rmax shares, rounded to lots, where rmax = min(max lots * round lot, fwork * workable shares, fhard * hard size). Only applied when hard size > 1.5*rmax and enough workable shares remain. Without the tag the values come from AlgoConfig, but only for algorithms in random_lotsize_algos (otherwise 0 = off).
tags.default: random_lotsize_max=5, random_lotsize_fhard=0.5, random_lotsize_fwork=0.05 (AlgoConfig) for algos in random_lotsize_algos, else 0

example.explanation: Jitter each candidate by at most 3 lots, 30% of hard size, 5% of workable shares.

interactions.title: Explicit 121 enables size randomisation for any algorithm
interactions.explanation: Setting the tag bypasses the AlgoConfig random_lotsize_algos check in the accessors, so randomisation applies even to algos where it is off by default.

tags.name: IIS email mode
tags.description: Integer flag stored as iis_email_mode; in the Java source it is only printed in the parameter summary. Its effect (presumably e-mail notifications for IIS orders) is not visible in the code read.

example.explanation: Set IIS email mode 1.

tags.name: Random min exec size
tags.description: Randomises the minimum execution quantity sent on child orders. The min exec size is drawn between min(min exec size, value) and the configured min exec size; mode 1 uses a uniform random draw, otherwise the draw is skewed by the order's participation progress. below_lot controls whether the result may fall below a round lot (1: below-lot values are kept or rounded up to one lot at random; 2: odd-lot min exec allowed).

allowedValues.meaning: skewed by accumulated participation rate vs min/max part levels
may go below a round lot / to 0, still round lot

example.explanation: Min exec randomly between 200 shares and the normal min exec size.

interactions.title: 123 only acts when a min exec size is already in effect
interactions.explanation: Randomisation runs only if param_minexecsize > 0 (from min exec / min exec value / dynamic min exec tag 142).

tags.name: Dark pool count
tags.description: Number of dark pools used in parallel. Either a plain integer, or an ADV-scaled form 'base,T,advM' giving count = max(3, ceil(stockADV/(advM*1e6 + stockADV) * base)); a value starting with 'T' uses AlgoConfig darkpool_count as base, a value ending in 'T' appends ',10'. Resolved per stock at setup and read by CandidateProcessor, ExchangeMaster, ConcertStrategy, IoIWorker and LCOddLotWorker.

example.explanation: Config base count scaled by ADV vs 10M.

tags.name: Use take-ping
tags.description: When > 0, the take worker also sets up TAKEPING venues (filtered by clean-pipe rules) before taking; if darkping mode (DPM) is 3 it uses DARKPING venues instead. Used in ConcertStrategy and NDMAStrategy.

example.explanation: Ping TAKEPING venues as part of taking.

interactions.title: DPM=3 switches take-ping to dark-ping venues
interactions.explanation: With use_takeping>0 and darkping_mode()==3 the engine uses AggressionLevel.DARKPING venues instead of TAKEPING (code comment: '9012=DPM=3^152=1^25=0' for GMO2).

tags.name: Cash price mode
tags.description: Selects the price used to value candidates in cash-balanced (portfolio) processing: 1 = strike last price (falls back to previous close) times FX, 3 = previous close times FX, otherwise the live last price times FX (strike/prev close if no quote).

example.explanation: Value cash legs at previous close.

tags.name: Input timezone mode
tags.description: Says which timezone the start/end times (9002/9003 etc.) are given in, so the engine converts them to the trading-server timezone. 1 = exchange local time, 2 = configured input timezone, 3 = GMT, or a timezone ID string (mode 4). An invalid ID leaves the timezone null and the order fails validation with 'invalid input time zone'.

example.explanation: Start/end times in the exchange's local time.

interactions.title: Bad timezone ID rejects the order
interactions.explanation: Modes >1 need a valid timezone; if the ID string does not match the resolved TimeZone, _input_timezone is null and checkForError() returns 'invalid input time zone'.

interactions.title: Rule disables open auction for orders starting after the open auction
interactions.explanation: ai.fixmsg.properties:309 sets 14=0 when a start time is given, 127 is not 3, and the start is at/after the earliest open auction.

interactions.title: FMRPOP AU rules set 127=1
interactions.explanation: Rules for clientAlgorithm FMRPOP in AU write 127=1 so their 9002=10:30:00 is read as local time.

tags.name: FX mode
tags.description: Controls FX handling for pair/cross-currency orders. Values <= 2 require pair spread units when the two legs have different currencies (otherwise the portfolio is rejected PAIRNEEDUNIT); > 2 skips that check; > 3 forces fx_rate to 1.0. Unset falls back to AlgoConfig fx_mode.

example.explanation: Ignore FX conversion.

interactions.title: Cross-currency pair without units is rejected
interactions.explanation: When fx_mode<=2 and the pair's currencies differ, checkPairUnits() may return an error and the portfolio is rejected with PAIRNEEDUNIT.

tags.name: Cash hold post mode
tags.description: For cash-balanced baskets: when the cash-balancing scale factor is ~0, hard and min sizes are always zeroed, but with a value > 0 the candidate keeps its max/workable (passive post) size instead of being zeroed.

example.explanation: Keep resting posts when cash balance halts the side.

tags.name: Cash lag side
tags.description: Marks which side of a cash-balanced basket is the lagging side: 1 = buy side lags, 2 = sell side lags, 0/3 other modes (>3 is coerced to 0). The lag side's candidates are scaled by the cash-balance ratio, get maxsize = hardsize, skip the regulator's part-rate check and are not added to CandidateRegulator; 0 makes the cash-balance step scale candidates with factor 0.

allowedValues.meaning: both sides scaled to 0 in cash balancing

example.explanation: Sell side follows the buy side.

tags.name: PEG limit / peg offset
tags.description: Either a plain peg limit value, or 'mode,delta' that shifts the PEG price more aggressively from the peg reference: mode 1 = delta bps of price, 2 = delta cents, 3 = delta ticks, 4 = delta fraction of the average spread, 5 = peg to midpoint. The plain value is exported as order info 'peg_limit' and is also the reference price used to convert a bps discretion in tag 132.

example.explanation: Peg one tick more aggressive than the peg level.

algorithmDependent.behavior: The offset is applied in PegWorker.computePegPrice only when algotype is PEG and mode 1-5.

interactions.title: Peg offset modes only work for PEG
interactions.explanation: computePegPrice applies the offset only if the order's algotype is PEG.

tags.name: PEG take discretion
tags.description: Discretion for a PEG order to take liquidity: the take price is the near-side (passive) price plus this amount; when that reaches the far touch the PEG takes. Parsed as BpsCps with default unit cents; converted to cents-per-share using the tag 131 value as the reference price. How much is taken depends on peg take mode (tag 186): 0 = stop peg and take all workable, 1 = take the peg candidate size, >1 = add a separate take candidate for the shares not pegged.

example.explanation: Take when the far side is within 2 cents of the peg's passive price.

interactions.title: Take behaviour depends on peg take mode 186
interactions.explanation: PegWorker.tryTake handles mode 0/1; with 186>1 ConcertStrategy.handlePEGTakeDiscretion adds a take candidate instead.

interactions.title: bps discretion without 131 converts to 0
interactions.explanation: Discretion is converted with cpsInDollar(_peg_limit); _peg_limit is the tag 131 value, so a bps-based discretion needs 131 set to a price.

tags.name: SOR duration
tags.description: SOR duration either as an integer or ADV-scaled 'base,T,advM' giving max(3, ceil(advM*1e6/(advM*1e6+stockADV) * base)); 'T' prefix uses AlgoConfig sor_duration_base (5). The resolved sor_duration() is only logged in the parameter summary; no consumer was found in the Java source.

example.explanation: Config base scaled by ADV vs 10M.

tags.name: Lag side aggression
tags.description: Double stored as lag_side_aggression (cash basket lag side). Only printed in the parameter summary; no consumer found in the Java source.

example.explanation: Lag side aggression 0.5.

tags.name: New shadow initial aggression
tags.description: Aggression used during a new-shadow order's initial phase: price = mid +/- min(1.5 * agg * spread, 0.5*spread + 2 ticks). Defaults to AlgoConfig newshadow_init_agg.

example.explanation: Start at the midpoint.

tags.name: Small quote size threshold
tags.description: If the far-side (inside aggressive) quote size is below this threshold, child orders to PMID/dark venues are capped at the passive price level from tag 137. The order accessor returns the tag value only (0 = off); AlgoConfig small_quote_size_thresh=500 is not used as a fallback by this accessor.

example.explanation: Below 1000 shares on the far side, cap dark prices at the passive level.

interactions.title: Uses 137 passive level
interactions.explanation: The cap price is small_quote_passive_level (tag 137, default AlgoConfig 'QUOTE').

tags.name: Small quote passive level
tags.description: Tick-price level (e.g. QUOTE) used to cap PMID/dark child prices when the far-side quote is smaller than tag 136.

example.explanation: Cap at the same-side quote.

interactions.title: 137 has no effect without 136
interactions.explanation: Only used when small_quote_size_thresh (136) > far-side quote size; 136 defaults to 0.

tags.name: Lead side rate
tags.description: Double stored as lead_side_rate (cash basket lead side). Only printed in the parameter summary; no consumer found in the Java source.

example.explanation: Lead side rate 0.1.

tags.name: Compound algo mode
tags.description: Selects how a COMPOUND order switches between the legs in 9060. 2/3 = time-based (CompoundTimeTracker; mode 2 drops the first leg if the stock has not opened); 1/7 = position (fill %) based, 7 measures against volume; 6 = split (COMPOUNDSPLIT); 5 = portfolio/pair tracker (appends 1=PAIR to legs); other numbers < 100 = price-based CompoundAlgoTracker; a non-numeric name = a named compound trigger from RelayScheduler (mode 100). Optional second field = stop leg index.

allowedValues.meaning: time based, drop first leg if pre-open

example.explanation: Switch legs by time as listed in 9060.

interactions.title: Unknown trigger name rejects
interactions.explanation: A non-numeric value that is not a known compound trigger sets _err_msg 'invalid compound algo mode tag139'.

interactions.title: Needs compound config 9060
interactions.explanation: Trackers are only built when _compound_config (from 9060) is set; otherwise no compound relay algorithm is created.

interactions.title: CIS / LADDER / STOPLOSS overwrite 139
interactions.explanation: convertCIS (IIS algos with 188) forces mode 3; convertLadder (197) and convertStopLoss (210) force mode 0 and rebuild the compound config.

interactions.title: Mode 2 skips first leg pre-open
interactions.explanation: With mode 2 the time tracker is adjusted by stock.opened(), so an order arriving before the open loses its first (auction) leg; docs recommend mode 3.

interactions.title: Mode 5 turns legs into PAIR
interactions.explanation: Subparameters get '^1=PAIR' appended and inherit pair tags; tag 62 defaults to the tracker's first threshold.

tags.name: PEG dark mode
tags.description: Lets a PEG order also use dark pools. 0 = regular peg, no dark; 1 = use dark with normal pricing (peg size halved to leave dark max size); 2 = use dark while pegging (dark and post limit = quote, dark orders treated out-of-money when outside the spread); 3 = same as 0.
tags.default: 0 in code; ai.fixmsg.properties:108 sets 1 for PEG when unset

example.explanation: PEG with dark pool participation.

interactions.title: Rule defaults PEG dark mode to 1
interactions.explanation: ai.fixmsg.properties:108 writes 140=1 for every PEG order without 140.

interactions.title: No dark (152) resets PEG dark mode to 0
interactions.explanation: When no dark worker is created (no_dark or no dark venues), ConcertStrategy resets peg_dark_mode to 0. E.g. HK short-sell SDMA converted to PEG gets 152=1 (line 6) and then 140=1 (line 108), which is reset.

tags.name: PEG post venue
tags.description: Forces the venue for peg candidates; with it set, PegWorker only sends a new order when it has no live orders (one live peg order at a time).

example.explanation: Post pegs only to that venue.

tags.name: Dynamic min exec size
tags.description: Overrides the child min exec size with min(value, floor(order size/500)*100), never above an existing min exec size.

example.explanation: Min exec up to 1000 shares, scaled by order size.

tags.name: Ninja2 post mode
tags.description: For shadow/ninja-like algos, a value > 0 enables lit posting (ninja2post): noPostLoud() returns false and PostWorker treats the order like ICENINJA for post-loud checks.

example.explanation: Let a NINJA-like order post on lit venues.

interactions.title: Only for shadow/ninja-like algos
interactions.explanation: ninja2post() requires algo().likeShadowNinja().

tags.name: Number of post layers
tags.description: Number of price layers used by the layered queue post worker (queue mode, tag 154>0). For non-scheduled algos without max participation it also multiplies the queue hard size. Defaults to OEO config num_post_layers.

example.explanation: Single layer queue.

interactions.title: Layers only used in queue mode
interactions.explanation: LayeredPostWorker is created only when queue_mode (154) > 0.

interactions.title: Rules default 144=1 in KS/China and for GRANTHAM/MK short-sell
interactions.explanation: Rules write 144=1 for KS and C1/C2/CH, GRANTHAM queue orders with low max part, and MK short-sell with 154=1.

tags.name: Cost save mode
tags.description: Integer exported in the order info map as 'cost_save_mode' (consumed outside this Java code). Default is 0 for cash baskets (doCash>0) and 1 otherwise.

example.explanation: Disable cost save mode.

tags.name: Honor end time (clean-up)
tags.description: When > 0, the engine finishes (cleans up) the leftover near the end time: if within the must-complete buffer of the end time (or, for non-scheduled algos, no fill for the stock wait time), open shares <= a clean-up threshold (config cleanup_pct/rls/aqs), within the participation cap and within the clean-up spread threshold (tag 185). Sends a CLEANUPLEFTOVER alert. Not applied when halted or passive-only no-take.

allowedValues.meaning: clean up leftover near end time

example.explanation: Take out small leftover before end time.

interactions.title: Rules enable 146 for VWAP/TMX
interactions.explanation: 146=1 is written for VWAP/TMX ending before continuous end (not short-sell, not APIL/APIM), SILK baskets without close, and IN orders with no max part and no close.

interactions.title: Passive-only no-take blocks clean-up
interactions.explanation: The clean-up branch requires !passive_only_notake(0).

tags.name: Include EOD candidate
tags.description: 0 removes candidates whose venue contains 'EOD' and disables purestream EOD mode 1. Default 0 for cash baskets, 1 otherwise.

example.explanation: No EOD venue candidates.

interactions.title: Disables purestream EOD mode 1
interactions.explanation: purestream_eod_mode() returns 0 when mode is 1 and include_eod_candidate()==0.

interactions.title: Rule sets 147=0 for prorate orders
interactions.explanation: ai.fixmsg.properties:505 writes 147=0^OCASH=0 when prorate_mode>0 (not APIL/APIM).

tags.name: Tilt parameters
tags.description: alpha,beta[,mode] stored as tilt_alpha/tilt_beta/tilt_mode. Accessors exist but no consumer was found in the Java source; meaning unknown (likely schedule tilt). Fewer than two fields throws a parse error.

example.explanation: Tilt alpha 0.1, beta 0.2, mode 1.

tags.name: More dark
tags.description: Integer exported in the order info map as 'more_dark' (consumed outside this Java code, presumably to favour dark venues).

example.explanation: Request more dark.

tags.name: Count dual-listed volume
tags.description: When > 0 and the stock has a dual listing, volume of the dual listing is included in market stats and the volume profile (vprof_sym becomes 'sym,dualSym'); opening logic may use the dual stock. Forced to >= 1 when dual trade (tag 202) is on or for the synthetic India router; forced to 0 if the stock has no dual listing.

example.explanation: Count volume on both IB and IS.

interactions.title: Dual trade forces 150 on
interactions.explanation: count_duallist_volume() returns max(value,1) when dual_trade()>0.

tags.name: Preempt volume mode
tags.description: When > 0 the order's market stats add 'preempt' volume (bid+ask size times config preempt_volume_quote_ratio, or 1-minute volume share) so participation sizing anticipates volume.

example.explanation: Anticipate volume.

tags.name: No dark
tags.description: When > 0 the order uses no dark pools: no dark (pmid) worker or dark-take pings are set up. Shadow algos then have no dark pool and are rejected NO_DARKPOOL unless they use IOIs exclusively; PEG dark mode is reset to 0.

example.explanation: Lit only.

interactions.title: Shadow with no dark is rejected
interactions.explanation: With no dark worker, a shadow algo not using IOI exclusively is rejected with NO_DARKPOOL.

interactions.title: HK short-sell SDMA becomes PEG with 152=1
interactions.explanation: ai.fixmsg.properties:6 converts HK short-sell SDMA to PEG and sets 152=1; the default 140=1 from line 108 is then reset to 0.

tags.name: Compound VWAP config
tags.description: Configuration string for the COMPOUNDVWAP client algorithm's CompoundVWAPTracker. Used only when the client algorithm is COMPOUNDVWAP and no other compound/scale/index tracker applies; an invalid string rejects with 'incorrect compound vwap tracker'.

example.explanation: Not documented in code read.

interactions.title: Invalid compound vwap string rejects
interactions.explanation: If the tracker built from 153 should not track, _err_msg='incorrect compound vwap tracker'.

interactions.title: Ignored when another compound tracker exists
interactions.explanation: COMPOUNDVWAP is the last branch of the relay-algorithm else-if chain.

tags.name: Queue mode
tags.description: Selects the posting worker. 0 = normal PostWorker; > 0 = layered queue worker (LayeredPostWorker, layers from tag 144) plus a simple post worker; < 0 = no post worker. 3 behaves as 2 when out of money else 1; 4 as 2 when outside spread else 1; >= 2 uses a shorter part-rate monitoring window. In queue mode passive-only 2 sets max size 0 and totalPassiveShares is 0.
tags.default: 0 in code; many rules set it

example.explanation: Queue with layered posts.

interactions.title: Rules default 154=1 for VWAP/PART but later rules reset to 0
interactions.explanation: Line 49 sets 154=1; later unguarded rules write 154=0 for C1/C2/CH, ICENINJA, IN, MAYBANK, APIH maxPartLevel<1 and HK/MK short-sell APIH (conflict C-17).

interactions.title: Queue + passive-only 2 zeroes max size
interactions.explanation: CandidateProcessor sets maxsize=0 when passive_only()==2 and queue_mode>0.

tags.name: Broker spec
tags.description: Restricts venues by broker/venue id per aggression level: '&'-separated entries 'AGGR1,AGGR2;BRK1,BRK2' or just 'BRK1,BRK2' (all levels), plus 'CHECKOFF;...' / 'IGNOREOFF;...' controlling whether venue shut-off/custom-venue checks still apply, and an EXCEPT key. Upper-cased; listed venues get their weight even if 0. When set, the normal enabled-exchange filtering (shut-off, primary-only) is skipped. Values like SG, HKEX, MAYBANK are used as conditions by many rules.

example.explanation: Take and post only via broker SG.

interactions.title: Broker spec bypasses venue shut-off and primary-only filters
interactions.explanation: enabledExchangesRaw returns all tradeable venues when broker_spec_map is set; shut-off checks only run for aggression levels marked CHECKOFF.

interactions.title: 155=SG drives many rule defaults
interactions.explanation: Rules key on 155=SG/HKEX/MAYBANK: skip LOR/LCR defaults when SG, set IN settings (MAXCD, ERB, PMS, TECT), 154=0^MWORK=1 for MAYBANK, HK short-sell DMAPPL/LORT/PPL for HKEX/SG.

tags.name: Grab mode
tags.description: Opportunistic 'grab' of liquidity: price,quotesize,shares[P][,aggr[,cap[,interval_sec]]]. price is a level (number, or ending in B/C/S, S needing a spread); quotesize may be SW/AW/BW/LW for sweep modes; shares ending in P is a percent of order, negative = mode 3; aggr is 0-1; cap may be prefixed C and suffixed P. Child orders are flagged with would-flag 6/7.

example.explanation: Grab up to 20% of the order when price is within 10 bps and size >= 500.

interactions.title: Invalid grab price rejects
interactions.explanation: A zero numeric grab price (unless allow_no_grab_price), or an S price without average spread, sets _err_msg and disables grab.

interactions.title: Rule sets 173=0 with grab
interactions.explanation: ai.fixmsg.properties:360 writes 173=0 to prevent dynamic passive-only when a grab is requested.

tags.name: Index tracker OOM mode
tags.description: Integer stored as the index-tracker out-of-money mode. In the available source it is only echoed in the parameter dump when an index tracker is configured; no engine logic reading indexTrackerOOMMode() was found.

example.explanation: Sets itk_oom_mode=1 (no visible effect in the source read).

tags.name: Broker-directed size
tags.description: Number of shares to direct to the broker list given in 163. 0 (or equal to the order size) means the whole order is broker-directed: venue selection is restricted to (or excludes, see 159) the listed brokers. A value between 0 and the order size splits the order into a BrokerDirect strategy for that many shares plus a normal strategy for the rest.

example.explanation: Direct 5,000 shares of a larger order to the brokers in 163; the remainder trades normally.

interactions.title: Broker-directed size above order size rejects
interactions.explanation: checkForError returns 'broker directed size > order size', which rejects the order.

interactions.title: Broker-directed size needs a broker list (163)
interactions.explanation: All broker-direct logic checks broker_direct_list(), which is built only from 163; without 163 the size has no effect.

interactions.title: Partial broker direction splits the order into two strategies
interactions.explanation: When 0 < 158 < order size a second strategy ('BrokerDirect') is created; BrokerDirectStrategy splits the goal so the directed strategy works up to 158 shares and the other works the rest.

tags.name: Broker-direct exclude
tags.description: Flips the meaning of the broker list in 163: 0 = only route to the listed brokers (exch.sbroker()), non-zero = route to every broker except the listed ones.

example.explanation: Never route to the brokers listed in 163.

interactions.title: Exclude flag needs a broker list (163)
interactions.explanation: The flag is only consulted when broker_direct_list() (built from 163) is non-null.

tags.name: PEG mode
tags.description: Integer PEG mode. In the source read it is only stored in the order-info map ('peg_mode') published by OrderHolder and in the parameter dump; no other engine logic was found.

example.explanation: Publishes peg_mode=1 in order info.

tags.name: Post layer price increment
tags.description: Overrides the increment used between posting layers in ConcertStrategy: when > 0 it replaces the default layer step 'a'.

example.explanation: Use 0.5 as the posting layer increment.

tags.name: Check open mode / OPE open mode
tags.description: Controls how the engine decides the stock has opened. Value < 10: check_open_mode, pushed onto the stock (setCheckOpenMode) if higher than the stock's current mode, and used to mark the stock open from an initial transaction. Value >= 10: tens digit = ope_open_mode (stock treated as opened ope_open_buffer ms after continuous/PM session start, buffer from 320; mode > 1 forces at least 1s), units digit = check_open_mode.

allowedValues.meaning: ope_open_mode=1, check_open_mode=0 (open by time buffer from 320)

example.explanation: Treat the stock as open once the 320 buffer has elapsed after the continuous session start.

interactions.title: OPE open mode uses 320 buffer to mark the stock open
interactions.explanation: With ope_open_mode > 0 the engine copies the stock and sets it opened/openedPM once now >= session start + ope_open_buffer (320, seconds).

interactions.title: Config sets 162=10 with a 320 buffer for most markets
interactions.explanation: ai.fixmsg.properties sets 162=10 plus 320=300 (TB), 180 (KS), 1 (MK/HK/C1/C2/CH/IN/PM/SP DMA algos) or 60 (all non-JP) when neither is set.

interactions.title: Raises the stock-wide check-open mode
interactions.explanation: If the stock is not open and this order's check_open_mode is higher than the stock's, it is stored on the stock via the security master, affecting other orders on the same stock.

tags.name: Broker-direct list
tags.description: Comma-separated list of broker codes (matched against exch.sbroker()) to direct the order to; parsed into broker_direct_list. Combined with 158 (how many shares) and 159 (include/exclude).

example.explanation: Route only to venues of brokers BRK1 and BRK2.

interactions.title: Restricts venue selection to (or away from) listed brokers
interactions.explanation: When 158 is 0 or equals order size, venues whose broker is not in the list are rejected (or, with 159!=0, listed brokers are rejected); strategy id becomes 'BrokerDirected'.

tags.name: MOO limit factor (sigma)
tags.description: Number of volatility sigmas used to set the limit price of market-on-open orders around the base price. 0 together with LOR (1527) = 0 means no MOO limit offset (limit from ticks only). If unset, per-market AlgoConfig moo_limit_factor; forced to 0 when the stock's mooPriceType is 2.

example.explanation: MOO limit = base price +/- 3 sigma.

interactions.title: Config zeroes MOO limit factor for most markets
interactions.explanation: ai.fixmsg.properties writes 164=0 and LOR=0 when LOR is not set, outside NZ/PM/IJ/MK/C1/C2/CH/HK; also for HK zero-price or HK short-sell non-ETF orders; NZ/PM/IJ/MK get 164=10, LOR=0.1. Note the rule does not check whether 164 itself was set, so a client 164 is overwritten.

interactions.title: Ignored when stock mooPriceType is 2
interactions.explanation: moo_limit_factor() returns 0 if the stock's mooPriceType()==2.

tags.name: Greedy mode
tags.description: When > 0, TakeWorker treats the order like a fully aggressive WOW order (takes liquidity when there is a limit price), and for WOW orders in the money ConcertStrategy returns 0 from the relevant size check.

example.explanation: Take aggressively whenever in the money.

tags.name: Cut-off (large print) size
tags.description: Per-order trade-size cutoff stored in Parameters.cutOffSize(). The engine's large-print filter is size_cutoff_multiplier (184) x order cutOffSize; prints larger than that (outside auctions) are excluded from the participation volume. Rules use 166=1000000000 to effectively disable filtering. Whether SysOrder.cutOffSize() reads this parameter could not be verified (SysOrder source not present).
tags.default: stock cutoff (9999/19999/39999 by region when absent)

example.explanation: Effectively disable large-print filtering.

interactions.title: Config adds 184=1 and 191=0.001 when 166 is set
interactions.explanation: Rules set 184=1 (multiplier 1) and 191=0.001 (quote multiplier negligible) when 166 is present and they are not, so the filter equals exactly the 166 size.

interactions.title: IPO orders get 166=1e9
interactions.explanation: IPO stocks get 184=1 and 166=1000000000 (no large-print filtering); also stocks with adv<1 and 184=1.

tags.name: Monitor period
tags.description: Monitoring period in seconds, with optional floor ('period,floor'). Only published in order info (monitor_period, monitor_period_flr) in the source read; consumed downstream.

example.explanation: Monitor period of 1.1 s.

interactions.title: Config sets 167=1 for APIH VWAP close orders, minimum 1.1
interactions.explanation: Rule sets 167=1 for VWAP with close in APIH near close; a later rule raises any monitor period between 0 and 1.1 to 1.1 (last writer wins).

tags.name: Leading volume mode
tags.description: When > 0, the average 1-minute volume is added as 'leading volume' to the volume estimates when the order market stats are updated (otherwise only on the first slice).

example.explanation: Always add the recent 1-minute volume as leading volume.

tags.name: Bps from low/high cap
tags.description: Caps the order price relative to today's range: buy limit = day high x (1 + bps/1e4), sell limit = day low x (1 - bps/1e4). Optional extra fields are aggression levels (e.g. dark, pmid); if any are listed the code sets an 'exception' flag that disables the low/high check entirely in withinLimit. Ignored when block_trade_filter > 0.

example.explanation: Cap at the day's high/low (0 bps); with aggression list given.

interactions.title: Config sets 169=0,dark,pmid for SHADOW
interactions.explanation: Non-fully-aggressive SHADOW orders get 169=0,dark,pmid by rule.

interactions.title: Aggression list disables the low/high price check
interactions.explanation: setBpsFromLowHigh sets _bps_from_low_high_exception=true when any aggression level is listed, and withinLimit only applies the cap when the exception flag is false.

tags.name: Staff ID
tags.description: Trader/staff identifier for the order. Used as traderID in published order maps, on portfolio client info, and in alerts (falls back to the system id when empty). May also be set from the configured staffid tag or client config.

example.explanation: Order attributed to trader JSMITH.

tags.name: Do PM open (afternoon opening auction)
tags.description: Participate in the afternoon (post-lunch) opening auction, analogous to 14 (open) and 15 (close). Ignored for stocks with no PM open. If there is no PM opening volume history and moopm_nohist is 0, the engine resets it to 0.

example.explanation: Send part of the order into the afternoon opening auction.

interactions.title: Config turns on PM open (171=1, OPEPMO=1) in JP/MK/TB/SP
interactions.explanation: Unless the client sets 171=0, rules enable PM open for most algos (and SHADOW/SHADOWMIN with min part level) in JP, MK, TB, SP.

interactions.title: AUCTIONS sets 14/15/171 together
interactions.explanation: AUCTIONS=0 writes 171=0, AUCTIONS=1 writes 171=1.

interactions.title: No effect where the stock has no PM open
interactions.explanation: doPMOpen() returns 0 if stock.noPMOpen().

interactions.title: IPO orders default 171=0
interactions.explanation: Rule writes 171=0 for IPOs when not set.

tags.name: Take venue selector
tags.description: Restricts TAKE allocations on 'ABOVE*' venues to a venue sub-type by id suffix: 3 -MMTAKE, 4 -MMSWPT, 5 -MMONLY, 6 -DSFTAKE (EU _SPDSFNICE), 7 -SWEEPOST, 8 -SWPSTDSF, 9 -AUTOROUTEDMA, 10 -SWPSTEOD, 11 -TAKE_MM, 12 -SWPST_MM, 13 -MMAUTOROUTEDMA, 14 EU dark sweep (_SPDSFNICE). In EU, 14 also keeps TAKE aggression for SHADOW/NINJA-like algos instead of downgrading to AGGR_PING.

example.explanation: Only take via SWEEPOST venues.

interactions.title: 172=14 keeps TAKE for EU shadow/ninja algos
interactions.explanation: adjustTAKE normally downgrades TAKE to AGGR_PING for EU likeShadowNinja algos; takeVenue 14 is the exception.

tags.name: Passive only
tags.description: Forbids taking and optionally other venue types. Value = mode*100 + level. Level: 1 no TAKE; 2 no TAKE, no pmid/dark; 3 no restriction in venue filter; 4 no pmid/dark; 5 no TAKE, no primary; 6 no TAKE/primary/pmid/dark; 7 no TAKE/pmid; 8 no TAKE/primary/pmid; 9 no pmid. With a portfolio dollar cap levels 1-10 become 11-20 (only round-lot TAKE blocked). Mode 0 (default) also zeroes min/hard candidate size; mode 1 (e.g. 101) keeps hard size.

example.explanation: Post only on lit venues, never take, no midpoint/dark.

interactions.title: HK short sells forced passive-only (173=2)
interactions.explanation: Rules write 173=2 (and 15=1 for VWAP/TMX, 15=0 otherwise) for HK non-ETF short sells, overriding any client 173.

interactions.title: Reg SHO restricted short sells set 173=1
interactions.explanation: Rule writes 173=1 and PPL=1 for short sells under Reg SHO restriction.

interactions.title: Grab mode (156) defaults 173=0
interactions.explanation: When 156 is set and 173 is not, rule sets 173=0.

interactions.title: 173=2 with queue mode zeroes max candidate size
interactions.explanation: If passive_only==2 and queue_mode (154) > 0, candidate maxsize is set to 0.

tags.name: Relay 9060 id
tags.description: String id stored as id_relay9060; no reader of id_relay9060() was found outside the accessor, so its effect is unknown.

example.explanation: Relay id R1 (effect not visible in source).

tags.name: Reload relay 9060
tags.description: When > 0, on a new (non-addition) fixmsg the engine reloads the algo relay map and fix-message config if the basket id, group id or 9001 changed since the last reload, or relay_reload_sleep ms elapsed.

example.explanation: Reload relay and ai.fixmsg config before applying them.

tags.name: Dark chunk size factor
tags.description: Caps the size of each dark/liquidity-seeking (LC) child order to dark_size x average trade size.

example.explanation: Dark child orders at most 2x the average trade size.

tags.name: Buy back
tags.description: Share buy-back order flag with optional exchange: '1' (US) or '2[,exch]' (EU, exchange defaults to the stock's exchange). Engine pulls end time 10/30 min before continuous end (mode 1), disables open/close custom tags, and caps size at buyback_max_limit x ADV minus already-bought (mode 2 also by the exchange's ADV).

example.explanation: EU buy back capped by XLON ADV.

interactions.title: Buy back on a sale rejects
interactions.explanation: checkForError: 'buy back on a sale'.

interactions.title: Buy back with auction participation rejects
interactions.explanation: checkForError: 'buy back participates in open or close auction' when doClose or doOpen > 0.

interactions.title: Region mismatch rejects
interactions.explanation: EU requires 177=2, NA requires 177=1; EU mode 2 rejects if no ADV for the buy-back exchange.

interactions.title: Buy back on stock without ADV/prevclose/market cap rejects
interactions.explanation: setBuyBackEndTime rejects when adv<1, no prev close, market cap<1, or the modified end time is before start.

tags.name: Max execution gap (minutes)
tags.description: If no fill has happened for more than this many (trading) minutes, the order regulator forces a catch-up goal of one round lot more.

example.explanation: Force a fill if 10 minutes pass without execution.

interactions.title: LINE/PASS default 178=10
interactions.explanation: Rule sets 178=10 for LINE and PASS when unset.

tags.name: Min lit participation level
tags.description: Minimum participation rate (percent) on lit volume. Validated against minpart_reject_min and against max lit part level; halved for large PART2 orders; split across sub-orders for split algos.

example.explanation: Participate at least 5% of lit volume.

algorithmDependent.behavior: Overwritten by the target lit participation level after 9012 parsing, and halved for large/small-cap PART2 orders.

interactions.title: Min lit > max lit rejects
interactions.explanation: checkForError: 'min lit part level > max lit part level' (also 'too small' below minpart_reject_min).

interactions.title: PART2 replaces 179 with target lit level
interactions.explanation: After parsing, PART2 sets _minlitpartlevel = _targetlitpartlevel.

interactions.title: Turns on large-print filter multiplier 1
interactions.explanation: size_cutoff_multiplier() defaults to 1.0 when min part or min lit part level > 0.

tags.name: Auction duration split (DT auction)
tags.description: Per-auction duration-dependent settings: groups separated by '&', each '[O|C|PO/PMO,...:]minutes_value,...,value' giving thresholds (order duration minutes) and values for open, close and PM-open auctions; the last entry without '_' applies to any longer duration. Parsed into open/close/pmopen dur_split/dur_value arrays.

example.explanation: Open/close value 1 if duration<=120 min, 3 if <=240, else 5.

interactions.title: TMX default auction split
interactions.explanation: Rule writes 180=O:120_1,240_3,5&C:120_1,240_3,5 for TMX/OPETMX.

tags.name: Synthetic iceberg mode
tags.description: Controls synthetic iceberg (engine-managed display) for orders with an iceberg size. >0 makes candidate size equal to the iceberg size and enables IcebergSOR/ICENINJA synthetic handling; 1 also trims a work order to its display size. If unset, AlgoConfig synthetic_iceberg_mode (default 1) applies only on synthetic_iceberg_markets (default GA).
tags.default: -1 -> AlgoConfig synthetic_iceberg_mode=1 on synthetic_iceberg_markets (GA), else off

example.explanation: Show only the iceberg display size, replenishing synthetically.

algorithmDependent.behavior: PostWorker uses tryIceNinja when iceberg size > 0 and mode > 0.

tags.name: Dark limit price mode
tags.description: 'mode[,range]' enabling a candidate-supplied dark limit price. Mode > 0: each candidate must carry a darklimit, otherwise its sizes are zeroed ('ignoring candidate with no dark limit'); IoI dark posting waits for a dark limit. Range is absolute or 'S<n>' = n x spread.

example.explanation: Require a dark limit from the candidate.

interactions.title: Sensato low-alpha large orders get 182=1
interactions.explanation: Sensato algo-wheel rules write 182=1 for large orders, so candidates without a dark limit will not trade.

tags.name: Lit limit price mode
tags.description: 'mode[,range]' enabling a candidate-supplied lit limit price. Mode > 0: candidates without a litlimit get zero size; PostWorker applies the lit limit. Range absolute or 'S<n>' x spread.

example.explanation: Require lit limit; range two spreads.

interactions.title: 387 without 183 breaks parsing
interactions.explanation: The 387 (second lit limit) block splits _lit_limit_price_str (183) instead of its own string, so 387 alone throws a NullPointerException and 387 always copies 183's mode.

tags.name: Size cutoff multiplier
tags.description: Multiplier for the large-print filter: prints larger than multiplier x cutoff size (166/stock) are excluded from participation volume (outside auctions). A value > 0 also marks the multiplier as tag-supplied so it beats the config use_size_cuttoff.
tags.default: AlgoConfig use_size_cuttoff=1; 1.0 when min part levels are set

example.explanation: Ignore prints larger than twice the cutoff size.

interactions.title: 184 overrides config use_size_cuttoff
interactions.explanation: With size_cutoff_intag>0 the tag multiplier is used before config use_size_cuttoff.

tags.name: Cleanup spread threshold
tags.description: Spread condition for end-of-order cleanup in ConcertStrategy: 'bps[,ticks]' (also '&'). Cleanup allowed only if spread <= ticks x tick size or < bps. Negative bps disables cleanup; 0 means always allowed.

example.explanation: Clean up only if spread <= 2 ticks or < 10 bps.

interactions.title: MFSIS converted to LINE with cleanup disabled
interactions.explanation: Rule writes ALGO=LINE, 185=-1 for 88=MFSIS.

tags.name: PEG take mode
tags.description: How a PEG order takes within its take discretion (132): 0 stop pegging and take all workable shares; 1 take the candidate size; >1 skips PegWorker take and uses ConcertStrategy handlePEGTakeDiscretion instead.

example.explanation: Take only the candidate size.

interactions.title: Needs a take discretion (132)
interactions.explanation: Both paths require peg_take_discretion_cps() > 0, derived from 132.

tags.name: PVWAP order start
tags.description: Integer stored as pvwap_order_start; only echoed in the parameter dump in the source read.

example.explanation: pvwap_order_start=1 (no visible effect).

tags.name: CIS switch time
tags.description: For IIS orders, switches to another algo at a time: '[T|unit,]time'. Converts the order into a compound time-tracked config (mode 3): IIS until the time, then the algo in 189 (default PCAP), copying all other 9012 tags.

example.explanation: Run IIS until 13:00 then switch to PCAP.

interactions.title: IIS converted to compound IIS -> 189 algo
interactions.explanation: convertCIS sets compound_algo_mode=3 and builds the compound config.

interactions.title: Malformed CIS time rejects
interactions.explanation: A single letter-led field (or unit with empty time) sets _err_msg 'Wrong CIS parameter'.

interactions.title: Ignored for non-IIS
interactions.explanation: convertCIS returns unless the algorithm is IIS.

tags.name: CIS switch algo
tags.description: Algo (and extra tags separated by '/') to switch to at the CIS time (188). Default PCAP.

example.explanation: Switch to VWAP with 6=10.

interactions.title: Needs 188
interactions.explanation: Used only by convertCIS, which needs 188 and IIS.

tags.name: Volume profile type
tags.description: Selects the volume profile model: 5, 10, 20 mapped to '05d', '10d', '20d' (days of history); other values used verbatim; 0 = default.

example.explanation: Use the 10-day volume profile.

tags.name: Size filter quote multiplier
tags.description: Raises the large-print filter to at least multiplier x average quote size. Beats config sizefilter_quote_multiplier (default 0); only applies when a size filter exists.

example.explanation: Filter >= 5x avg quote size.

interactions.title: Config sets 191=0.001 when 166 is set
interactions.explanation: Keeps the filter equal to the explicit cutoff.

tags.name: Must EOD
tags.description: End-of-day completion: 'mode[,lead_ms]'. >0 at EOD lets the order work the full scheduler size; 2/3 disable taking at EOD and keep posts until close; 3 also sizes EOD orders to all available shares. Lead time (ms) overrides the EOD venue buffer (EODBN/1685).

allowedValues.meaning: no take at EOD, post to close
as 2 plus EOD orders use all available

example.explanation: Finish via EOD venue, buffer 10 s.

interactions.title: Lead time overrides EODBN; modes 2/3 override SPB
interactions.explanation: eod_venue_buffer_min() returns lead time first; postpool_zero_before_close() returns 0 for 2/3.

tags.name: Opportunistic finish
tags.description: Finish at the inside price when conditions hold (Statics.checkOpportunisticFinishChance, not in source): 'mode[,dollar_limit|price][,percent_order][,bps]'. Mode 4 takes a price. Defaults from AlgoConfig maps (dollar '2 5e4', percent '3 50').

example.explanation: Opportunistically finish with config limits.

interactions.title: FMRPOP/KSPOP rules set 193=2
interactions.explanation: Client-algo rules write 193=2 with LINE.

tags.name: Dark venue flag (randomisable)
tags.description: Integer stored as darkVenue. Values >=100 are randomised at parse time: with probability (value-100)% the flag becomes 1, otherwise 0 (A/B switch). No reader of darkVenue() was found in the engine source, so the flag currently has no visible effect.
tags.valueFormat: int (0/1, or 100+p for p% random chance of 1)

example.explanation: 50% chance the flag is set to 1.

tags.name: Dark mid-price mode
tags.description: When >0, dark/mid-point child prices are not snapped to the venue tick grid on venues that allow off-tick prices (offTickMode>0), so true mid prices can be sent; also NEWSHADOW dark limits are shifted by half a tick and would-dark orders without IOI skip a price check. When 0, prices are rounded to the closest valid tick.

allowedValues.meaning: allow off-tick mid prices on off-tick venues

tags.default: 0 in code; ai.fixmsg.properties:371 sets 195=1 for every order whose algorithm is not MOO/MOC/PAIR when unset

example.explanation: Send dark orders at exact mid-price where the venue supports off-tick prices.

algorithmDependent.behavior: dark limit moved half a tick more aggressive (LCWorker.java:671)

interactions.title: Rule defaults 195=1
interactions.explanation: ai.fixmsg.properties:371 sets 195=1 on all non MOO/MOC/PAIR orders that do not carry 195, so off-tick mid pricing is effectively the default.

interactions.title: Only effective on off-tick venues
interactions.explanation: Tick snapping is skipped only if the venue/exchange offTickMode>0; otherwise prices are still rounded.

tags.name: Start take mode
